title: Explaining a staged infant treatment plan
summary: Your infant son was diagnosed on day 24 through newborn screening and confirmatory testing with severe mucopolysaccharidosis type II. An IDS variant and undetectable relevant enzyme activity were found.
purpose: Audience: the infant’s parents. Use 220–280 words in plain English. Explain to the parents why the team is considering more than one treatment route, why treatment is staged, and what the plan cannot guarantee. Describe the broad risks and questions to discuss with the specialist team in accessible language. Do not give procedural instructions or promise a particular developmental outcome. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.

case.title: Explaining a staged infant treatment plan
case.opening: Your infant son was diagnosed on day 24 through newborn screening and confirmatory testing with severe mucopolysaccharidosis type II. An IDS variant and undetectable relevant enzyme activity were found.
case.initial_facts:
Your infant son was diagnosed on day 24 through newborn screening and confirmatory testing with severe mucopolysaccharidosis type II. An IDS variant and undetectable relevant enzyme activity were found.
Intravenous enzyme replacement began at two months, and enzyme delivery into the brain’s fluid spaces began at three months. The specialist team is preparing a cord-blood transplant at nine months, after growth and donor coordination. The paper’s rationale is that blood-delivered treatment and transplant do not address brain involvement equally well in type II disease. Transplant outcomes, later development and complications are not yet available at this task’s decision point.

case.hidden: Infant 3 later had mild sinusoidal obstruction, a SARS-CoV-2 infection, no acute GVHD, and resumed brain-directed enzyme treatment on day 47. Follow-up outcomes, including developmental quotient, were not supplied. The prompt is a retrospective pretransplant adaptation, not a claim that all infants share these outcomes.
case.reference: Explain the missing-enzyme problem and the different access of systemic versus brain-directed treatment without implying identical effects in every mucopolysaccharidosis subtype. The stated growth/donor-coordination interval can be explained without inventing a universal optimal transplant age. Acknowledge transplant/procedure risks and uncertain long-term development; do not assume transplant outcomes or later development. Keep jargon explained and avoid a personalised guarantee or instructions to change treatment.
